Materials Science and Engineering & X Double Major Programme

Materials Science and Engineering & X Double Major Programme

Applicable to students admitted in 2025-26

 

 

Major Programme Requirement

Students are required to complete a minimum of 90 units of courses. Students will take the Materials Science and Engineering offered by CUHK as the 1st Major, and choose from one of the Majors offered by CUHK or CUHK(SZ) as specified in 3. below as their 2nd Major. Some courses offered by CUHK and CUHK(SZ) are substitute/equivalent/alternative courses. Please refer to the list of substitute/equivalent/alternative courses for details.

Students are required to take a total of 27 units of elective courses from the area which corresponds to the 2nd Major chosen by them.

6-15 units to be taken from Group A, and 12-21 units from Group B, of which at least 12 units of courses should be from 3000 or above level (including at least 6 units of courses at 4000 level).

Explanatory Notes:

1.

Students enrolled in the Double Major Programme should normally spend four regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study, except otherwise specified in 2. below. It applies to all students, including those who select a 2nd Major offered by CUHK.

2.

Students who join term-time exchange programme have to spend at least three regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study.

3.

Students enrolled in the Double Major programme can take substitute/equivalent/alternative courses either at CUHK or CUHK(SZ). The list of substitute/equivalent/alternative courses is available at this link (https://mase.erg.cuhk.edu.hk/programme-information). Students should not take a course and its substitute/equivalent/alternative course. Should they do so, only one course will be counted towards the fulfillment of units requirements. Grades of relevant substitute/equivalent/alternative courses taken at CUHK(SZ) will be transferred to CUHK for the purpose of calculation of GPA, Major GPA and credit units.

4.

Students normally have to declare their 2nd Major by the end of their first year of study.

5.

All courses at 2000 and above level and courses labeled as # in the requirements of the 1st Major Programme, courses labelled as # in the requirements of the 2nd Major, as well as 3 or 4 units of research component course offered by the 2nd Major, will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

6.

Courses taken to fulfill the requirements of the 1st Major cannot be counted towards the fulfillment of requirements of the 2nd Major, and vice versa.

7.

Under very special circumstances and subject to approval by the Major programmes concerned, students may opt out of the Double Major Programme and register for the Materials Science and Engineering Programme offered by CUHK as single major. The decision to opt out is irrevocable. Students who have opted out are required to complete and fulfill all graduation requirements by following the study scheme of the Materials Science and Engineering Programme as a single major and spend the remaining course of study at CUHK.  Students should be aware that such decisions may result in a delay in graduation because the requirements of the single major study scheme differ from those of the Double Major Programme.

[a]

Students taking Physics or Chemistry offered by CUHK as 2nd Major should take MATH1010.

[b]

Students taking Physics or Chemistry offered by CUHK as 2nd Major should take PHYS1111.

Students may apply to study in the Co-operative Education Programme (Co-op@CUHK) (5 units) in Year 2 or above. Students who study the Co-op programme will take COOP4001, which is a 1-unit course to be taken in each of the Summer Session of Year 3 and Term 1 of Year 4. They will undertake a full-time placement in two specific work terms, during which they are not allowed to register for any other courses except the 1-unit continuous assessment course COOP4001. For students who have to take more than 1 unit of course in the work term, they should provide strong justifications for each additional course for approval by the Co-operative Education Programme Committee and the major programme.

[b]

When students are studying at CUHK(SZ), they can take substitute/equivalent/alternative courses at CUHK(SZ) to fulfill the requirements of CUHK.

[c]

The recommended course pattern of College GE courses varies according to student’s college affiliation.

[d]

Approval has been granted by the Registrar for students of the Materials Science and Engineering & X Double Major Programme to take 19 units of courses in Term 1 and/or Term 2 of Year 1.

Study Scheme
Learning Outcomes
 

1. Major Programme:

 

Upon completion of the programme, students will be able to:

 

(i)

explain the scientific principles and methods underlying the study and application of traditional and modern materials (K);

(ii)

demonstrate an understanding across a wide range of materials-related topics in chemistry, physics, electronic engineering, mechanical engineering, energy and environment (K);

(iii)

apply knowledge of natural sciences, engineering, and computing appropriate to develop solutions to complex problems related to materials (K/S);

(iv)

design innovative and sustainable materials-related technology solutions to meet identified needs with appropriate economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, cultural, health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, manufacturability considerations as required (S/V);

(v)

conduct investigations of complex scientific and engineering problems using research-based knowledge, design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions (K/S);

(vi)

analyze and evaluate the impact of engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental and societal context, especially the importance of health, safety, legal, and sustainable considerations (S/V);

(vii)

apply ethical principles, commit to professional ethics and norms of engineering practice and adhere to relevant national and international laws with the understanding of the need for diversity and inclusion (K/V);

(viii)

communicate effectively and inclusively on scientific and engineering activities, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations (S/V); and

(ix)

stay abreast of contemporary issues and recognize the need for independent and life-long learning, adaptability to new and emerging technologies, and critical thinking in the context of technological change (K/S).

 

 

 

 

K = Knowledge outcomes

S = Skills outcomes

V = Values and attitude outcomes
